options.text: to guess that it is being the aeroplane

Key Points

questions.question: Select the most appropriate collocation to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. We congratulated him at his new job. He was delighted.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate collocation to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

We congratulated him at his new job. He was delighted.
questions.solution: The correct answer is "congratulated him on". Congratulated him on: to compliment someone and express approval or happiness on a noteworthy or exceptional accomplishment. Example: He congratulated me on my wedding. It is apparent from the explanation that "congratulated him on" is an appropriate collocation instead of "congratulated him at".

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. It is reported that she has win a prize money of ten lakhs at a reality show.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

It is reported that she has win a prize money of ten lakhs at a reality show.
questions.solution: In the given sentence, the verb form is used incorrectly. The sentence is in present perfect tense thus the past participle of the verb "win" should be used. Thus, the correct phrase to use instead is "she has won."

questions.question: Correct the underlined part of the sentence. This mango is bitterer.
questions.questionHtml:
Correct the underlined part of the sentence.

This mango is bitterer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The underlined part of the sentence, "bitterer," is incorrect because it uses the comparative form inappropriately.
  • The sentence implies a simple description of the mango's taste, not a comparison between two or more mangoes.
  • For a simple description, the base form of the adjective should be used.
  • Therefore, the correct form of the adjective in this context is "bitter."
Therefore, the correct answer is 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "This mango is bitter."
 
Additional Information
  • 1) most bitter – This is the superlative form, indicating the highest degree of bitterness among three or more items. It's not suitable for describing a single mango.
  • 2) more bitter – This is the comparative form, used to compare the bitterness of two items. The sentence doesn't suggest a comparison.
  • 3) bitterest – This is another superlative form, similar to "most bitter," and is also inappropriate for describing a single item without comparison.

questions.question: Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution'. One must do his work .

The possessive pronoun "one's" agrees with the subject "One" and ensures grammatical consistency. "His work" is incorrect as it introduces gender-specific language.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Abu said that he saw the picture .

Abu said that he saw the picture.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The painting look good in this room.

Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The painting look good in this room.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: looks. The subject "The painting" is singular, so the verb must be in the singular form "looks" to ensure subject-verb agreement in the present tense.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The chair I have bought recently is costly than what I bought last year.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The chair I have bought recently is costly than what I bought last year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
Key Points
  • The underlined segment "is costly" needs to be replaced with a comparative form to correctly convey the comparison being made.
  • The correct comparative form of "costly" is "costlier."
  • The sentence should read, "The chair I have bought recently is costlier than what I bought last year."
Therefore, the correct answer is 2.
 
Correct Sentence: "The chair I have bought recently is costlier than what I bought last year."
 
Additional Information
  • 1: "is the costliest" – This implies a superlative comparison, which is not suitable here as the comparison is between two items.
  • 3: "was costly" – This changes the tense and does not provide the necessary comparative structure.
  • 4: "will be costly" – This changes both the tense and the comparative meaning, making it incorrect.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The housing loan taken by Ramesh effected his daily expenses adversely.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The housing loan taken by Ramesh effected his daily expenses adversely.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: by Ramesh affected. The word "affected" is the correct form to use here as it means to have an impact on something, whereas "effected" means to bring about or cause something to happen.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Next month, she was going to the institute to study for a master's degree.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Next month, she was going to the institute to study for a master's degree.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) is going to.

 Key Points

  • The phrase "next month" indicates a future action.
  • We "is going to" to indicate an action that will take place in the future.
    • Example: We are going to attend the party next week.
  • This means that the action is planned or intended to happen in the future.

Therefore, the correct sentence is  Next month, she is going to the institute to study for a master's degree. 

Additional Information

  • Option 1) "went to" is in the past tense and is not appropriate in this context.
  • Option 2) "has gone to" is in the present perfect tense, which implies that the action is already completed, and is not appropriate in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. When it started raining, I ran to the nearer house for shelter.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

When it started raining, I ran to the nearer house for shelter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. the nearest house

The sentence refers to only one house, the term 'nearer' is a comparative term which is used only where there are 2 entities to compare. Thus, the sentence needs to replace 'nearer' with a superlative term 'nearest'.

Thus, the correct answer is option 4.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segments in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute them, select ‘No substitution required’. The lockdowns has give many parents and grandparents the opportunity to share some of my nostalgic memories with their children and grandchildren.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segments in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute them, select ‘No substitution required’.

The lockdowns has give many parents and grandparents the opportunity to share some of my nostalgic memories with their children and grandchildren.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'have given; of their'.

Key Points

  • The underlined part is incorrectly used.
  • In the first underlined part 'have given' should be used because we know that in a sentence a verb should be used according to its subject.
  • Here, 'the lockdowns' is plural. Hence, a plural helping verb should be used. 
  • We know that 'have' is followed by the past participle. Hence, 'give' should be changed into 'given'.
  • In the second underlined part 'of their' should be used because 'their' is used for plural nouns. In the given sentence it is referring to 'parents and grandparents'.
     

Correct Sentence: The lockdowns have given many parents and grandparents the opportunity to share some of their nostalgic memories with their children and grandchildren.

Hinglish

  • रेखांकित भाग का गलत उपयोग किया गया है।
  • पहले रेखांकित भाग में 'have given' का प्रयोग करना चाहिए क्योंकि हम जानते हैं कि एक वाक्य में एक क्रिया का प्रयोग उसके विषय के अनुसार करना चाहिए।
  • यहां 'the lockdowns' plural है। इसलिए, एक बहुवचन helping verb का उपयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
  • हम जानते हैं कि past participle द्वारा 'have' का अनुसरण किया जाता है। इसलिए, 'give' को 'given' में बदल देना चाहिए।
  • दूसरे रेखांकित भाग में 'their' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए क्योंकि बहुवचन संज्ञाओं के लिए 'their' प्रयोग होता है। दिया गया वाक्य 'parents and grandparents' की बात कर रहा है।

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Either you and my sister is involved in this crime.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Either you and my sister is involved in this crime.
questions.solution: In the given options, "you or my" can improve the given part of sentence. We use "Either-or" in affirmative sentences to express a cause-and-effect relationship or to indicate a choice between two possibilities. Example: You can stay either with me or with Janet.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The government is developing a new test in the recruitment and training of teachers in the upcoming session.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The government is developing a new test in the recruitment and training of teachers in the upcoming session.

options.text: in recruitment and training on teachers
options.html: in recruitment and training on teachers

options.text: of the recruitment and training of teachers
options.html: of the recruitment and training of teachers

options.text: for the recruitment and training of teachers
options.html: for the recruitment and training of teachers

options.text: for recruitment or training of teachers
options.html: for recruitment or training of teachers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. for the recruitment and training of teachers .

Key Points

  • The preposition "for" is the most appropriate choice when expressing the purpose or intention of an action, which is applicable in this context.
  • The phrase "for the recruitment and training of teachers" clearly conveys the purpose of the test being developed by the government.
  • Other prepositions like "in", "of", or "on" do not convey the intended meaning as accurately as "for."

Correct sentence: The government is developing a new test for the recruitment and training of teachers in the upcoming session.

Additional Information

  • Usage of Prepositions:
    • For: Indicates purpose or intention. Example: This is a tool for cutting wood.
    • In: Indicates inclusion or location. Example: She is in the room.
    • Of: Indicates possession or relation. Example: The tail of the dog is wagging.
    • On: Indicates position or surface. Example: The book is on the table.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. He has set up his business now as he knows the ins and outs of it .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

He has set up his business now as he knows the ins and outs of it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

The idiom the ins and outs means the details of something. The sentence means that he knows the details of his business.

Few examples:

It takes some time to learn the ins and outs of this chapter.

Shanu knows the ins and outs of repairing computers.

So the correct answer is option 1.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No substitution required. The two sisters look quite different in each other .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No substitution required.

The two sisters look quite different in each other.
questions.solution: The correct answer is "different from each other". The adjective different means ‘not the same’. When we compare two or more items, it is usually followed by 'from'.​ Example: Adam is so different from his brother.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’. His claim to be the smartly kid in the school was a bit hyperbole!
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2)

Key Points

  • The phrase "the smartly kid" is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, "smartest" is the superlative form of the adjective "smart."
  • The superlative form is used when comparing three or more items, in this case, the student to the rest of the school.
  • Correct usage would be: "His claim to be the smartest kid in the school was a bit hyperbole!"
  • “Smartest” correctly fits the context of the sentence while adhering to grammatical rules.
  • The context implies he is claiming to be the best in terms of intelligence compared to others.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.

Additional Information

  • No rectification needed – This implies the original sentence is correct, which it is not.
  • Smarter – This is the comparative form, but superlative is needed for the context.
  • Smart – This is the base form, but doesn’t fit the context of the sentence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. They have been living here during ten years.

They have been living here during ten years.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement. The Finance Minister has announce big schemes for farmers, women and unorganized workers in his Budget speech.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.

The Finance Minister has announce big schemes for farmers, women and unorganized workers in his Budget speech.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 2 i.e. has announced.

Explanation

  • 'has announce' is wrong because whenever we use has/have/had, the main verb must be in its past participle form. 
  • Here, the verb is 'announce' whose past participle is 'announced'. 
  • So, 'has announced' is the correct word. 
  • 'have announced' is wrong because 'Finance Minister' is singular and 'have' is used for plurals nouns. 
  • 'has been announcing' is incorrect as the passive form is not required in the sentence

The correct sentence-The Finance Minister has announced big schemes for farmers, women and unorganized workers in his Budget speech.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. It is not wise relying to anybody too much.

In the given sentence, the first mistake to be noticed is preposition and then the verb form which is wrong too.

The correct sentence will be as follows:

It is not wise to rely on anybody too much.

One can also notice that in option 1 and option 2 has mistakes in the preposition part.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’ . No sooner I get the message, I shall pass it on to you.

No sooner I get the message, I shall pass it on to you.
questions.solution: The first part is in the present tense while the second part is in the future tense. Since we are talking about an event in the future. it will be suitable to use the conjunction 'as soon as'. Hence the correct sentence is: As soon as I get the message, I shall pass it on to you.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. Pedestrians is to be careful when crossin g busy roads.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

Pedestrians is to be careful when crossing busy roads.

options.text: would care if they are crossing
options.html: would care if they are crossing

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. must be careful when crossing.

Firstly, Pedestrians is a plural subject. So, the verb accompanying it should also be plural. But here, the singular verb ‘is’ is used. 

We have to replace the underlined phrase with ‘must be careful when crossing’. You use ‘must’ to indicate that you think it is very important or necessary for something to happen. 

Eg: She must take good care of the patient.

The other options are grammatically incorrect. 

Correct sentence: Pedestrians must be careful when crossing busy roads.

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. She is taking all kinds of medicine wherever she goes.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

She is taking all kinds of medicine wherever she goes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'takes'.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the use of the present continuous form of the verb "is taking" is incorrect.
  • The verb 'goes' indicates that the given sentence is in the simple present tense. 
  • We use the simple present tense when an action is happening right now, or when it happens regularly.
  • The third-person singular present form of the verb 'takes' should be used in place of "is taking".


Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct Sentence: She takes all kinds of medicine wherever she goes.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence. I hope you break a leg at your performance tonight!
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I hope you break a leg at your performance tonight!
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3)

Key Points

  • The phrase "break a leg" is an idiom that means to wish someone good luck. (किसी को शुभकामनाएं देने के लिए प्रयुक्त एक मुहावरा)
    • Example: Before the big show, everyone told the actor to break a leg.
  • Perform well refers to executing a task or role at a high standard. (अच्छा प्रदर्शन करना)
    • Example: The students are expected to perform well in their examinations.
  • Hence, we can infer that the phrase "break a leg" is a way to wish someone to perform well.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Perform well.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Give up (त्याग देना): To stop trying or to surrender.
    • Example: She decided not to give up despite the difficulties.
  • Make a mistake (गलती करना): To do something incorrectly or inaccurately.
    • Example: It’s natural to make a mistake when you’re learning something new.
  • Hurt yourself (स्वयं को चोट पहुंचाना): To cause physical pain or injury to oneself.
    • Example: Be careful with that knife, or you might hurt yourself.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. The children have been quarrelling all the time, are they ?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

The children have been quarrelling all the time, are they?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "haven't they"

Key Points

  • According to grammar, whenever we use a question tag then, we need to take it according to the main verb of the sentence. In the given sentence, the main verb is "have" hence, we need to use a question tag "haven't" and the pronoun will be used according to the subject of the sentence i.e. "they".
  • Hence, the correct answer is Option 2 i.e. "Haven't they"

So the correct sentence is- The children have been quarrelling all the time, haven't they?

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Gourav was no good than a foolish person.

Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Gourav was no good than a foolish person.

The correct answer is: no better

The phrase "no better than" is grammatically correct because it properly compares two things, implying that Gourav and a foolish person are of the same level.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. Rishi Sunak, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and Leader of the Conservative Party, was born into Southampton to parents of Indian descent who immigrated to Britain from East Africa in the 1960s.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

Rishi Sunak, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and Leader of the Conservative Party, was born into Southampton to parents of Indian descent who immigrated to Britain from East Africa in the 1960s.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. was born in .

Key Points

  • The given sentence provides biographical information about Rishi Sunak, specifying his birthplace and his parents' heritage.
  • The phrase "was born into Southampton" is incorrect. The correct preposition to use with "born" when referring to a place is "in".
  • Therefore, the correct substitution for the underlined segment is "was born in".

Correct sentence: Rishi Sunak, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and Leader of the Conservative Party, was born in Southampton to parents of Indian descent who immigrated to Britain from East Africa in the 1960s.

Additional Information

  • Common Prepositions with "Born":
    • Born in: Used to indicate the place of birth. Example: She was born in London.
    • Born on: Used to indicate the date of birth. Example: He was born on July 4th.
    • Born to: Used to indicate the parents. Example: She was born to a famous actor.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. One of the rooms in the new house had not yet been completed.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

One of the rooms in the new house had not yet been completed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'has not yet been'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'has not yet been' should be used instead of 'had not yet been'.
  • We use "yet" as an adverb to refer to a time that starts in the past and continues up to the present.
  • Adverbs of the present perfect tense are yet, already, just, recently, lately, ever, and never. They are commonly used in Present Perfect sentences to express the regularity or continuity of an action or activity. 
    • Example: They have already arrived.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 3.
     

Correct Sentence: One of the rooms in the new house has not yet been completed.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement Sonia is learnt to play the guitar these days.

Sonia is learnt to play the guitar these days.

The use of 'these days' indicate that the action has not been completed yet and is in the process of being performed. So, we will use the continuous form of the verb.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'. While he saw the bear , he ran to the nearest tree, dropped his gun and climbed to a safe place.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

While he saw the bear, he ran to the nearest tree, dropped his gun and climbed to a safe place.
questions.solution: "While" typically emphasizes simultaneous actions without strongly indicating a cause-and-effect relationship, whereas "when" is used to highlight a specific trigger event that leads to a subsequent action. In the given sentence, "When" is a more suitable choice because it establishes that the sighting of the bear prompted the person to take immediate action.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. UNICEF builds partnerships across the global community on accelerate gender equality.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

UNICEF builds partnerships across the global community on accelerate gender equality.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: global community to accelerate.

The marked option is correct grammatically because "to accelerate" correctly uses the infinitive form of the verb to indicate the purpose of building partnerships.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Food prices in Switzerland are as expensive to the rest of Western Europe.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Food prices in Switzerland are as expensive to the rest of Western Europe.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. more expensive than .

Key Points

  • The given sentence compares food prices in Switzerland with the rest of Western Europe, which requires the use of the comparative degree of the adjective.
  • The correct comparative form of "expensive" is "more expensive than", as it is a multi-syllable adjective that forms its comparative with "more" instead of "-er".
  • The phrase "as expensive to" is incorrect because "to" is not used for making comparisons; "than" is the correct preposition for comparison.
  • Option 1 ("the most expensive than") is incorrect because "the most expensive" is the superlative degree, which is used to compare one item with all others in a group, not just two entities.
  • Option 4 is incomplete and does not form a proper comparative structure.

Correct sentence: Food prices in Switzerland are more expensive than the rest of Western Europe.

Additional Information

  • Comparative Degree:
    • Used to compare two entities.
    • Formed by adding "-er" to short adjectives (e.g., taller, bigger) or using "more" with longer adjectives (e.g., more beautiful, more expensive).
  • Superlative Degree:
    • Used to compare one entity with a group.
    • Formed by adding "-est" to short adjectives (e.g., tallest, biggest) or using "most" with longer adjectives (e.g., most beautiful, most expensive).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Gel ingredients work well on waved, curled, relax and texture hair in the long run.

Gel ingredients work well on waved, curled, relax and texture hair in the long run.
questions.solution: Here, 'relaxed and textured' should be used instead of 'relax and texture'. The given sentence is in the simple past tense. The simple past tense, sometimes called the preterite, is used to talk about a completed action in a time before now.

Here, 'No sooner had he got out of her sight than' should be used instead of 'No sooner had he got out of her sight that'. We know that 'No sooner' is followed by 'than'. Correct Sentence: No sooner had he got out of her sight than she proceeded to tamper with the letter.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. While travelling, one comes across the larger number of people.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

While travelling, one comes across the larger number of people.
questions.solution: The correct answer is "a large number of". The phrase "a large number of" is used when referring to many people or things. It's an indefinite determiner, followed by a plural noun. The article "a" is used because "large number" begins with a consonant sound. The use of "the" would imply a specific large number, which is not what is intended here.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required.’ Our school has been issued instructions to restrict online classes to two hours towards the primary classes.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required.’

Our school has been issued instructions to restrict online classes to two hours towards the primary classes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'for.'
Key Points
  • When we read the sentence, we get to know there is a mistake related to prepositions.
  • For means intended to be given to.
  • For Examples:- 
    • There's a phone message for you.
    • I'd better buy something for the new baby.
    • There's a prize for the fastest three runners in each category.
  • Towards means in the direction of, or closer to someone or something.
  • For Examples:- 
    • ​She stood up and walked towards him.
    • He leaned towards his wife and whispered, "Can we go home soon?"
  • For will be used in the given sentence because the online classes were intended to be given to the primary classes.
  • Hence, the correct answer is Option 2.
     
So, the sentence would be - Our school has been issued instructions to restrict online classes to two hours for the primary classes.
Additional Information
  • Let's understand the concept with some more examples.
  • He has been playing cricket for two hours.
  • I have known him for ten years.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The manager asked me if I have completed my projects .

The correct answer is '3' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • In the second part of the given sentence, the singular form of the verb 'have' is incorrect.
  • The verb form "had" is used because the sentence is in the past perfect tense.
  • The manager's question about the completion of projects refers to an action that was completed before another action in the past (the moment the manager asked).
  • Hence, "had completed" correctly indicates that the projects were finished prior to being asked.
  • Therefore, the past perfect form of the verb 'had' should be used in place of the present perfect form 'have'.

Correct sentence: The manager asked me if I had completed my projects.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Simon is afraid of closed space .

Simon is afraid of closed space.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is  Option 3)

Key Points

  • Claustrophobia is the fear of closed or confined spaces.
  • Claustrophobia is commonly experienced in elevators, small rooms, and crowded areas.
  • It is a type of anxiety disorder and can be treated with therapy and counseling.
  • People with claustrophobia often avoid places and situations where they might feel trapped or confined.​.

  • Xenophobia is the fear of strangers or foreigners.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I had not only helped her by giving hints but also with providing her links.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
I had not only helped her by giving hints but also with providing her links.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The phrase "not only... but also" is used to connect two related actions, emphasizing that both actions were done.
  • The correct format for this phrase in the sentence is: "helped her not only by giving hints but also by providing her links."
  • Thus, the most appropriate substitution is helped her not only by.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "I had helped her not only by giving hints but also by providing her links."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: "helped her not by" – This changes the intended meaning of the sentence and does not use the "not only... but also" structure correctly.
  • Option 3: "helped her only by" – This implies that helping was limited to one action and does not reflect the intended emphasis of doing more than one thing.
  • Option 4: "helped not only her by" – This is incorrect because it disrupts the proper structure and meaning of the phrase "not only... but also."

questions.question: Direction: Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct. The dress is too tights around the waist.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The dress is too tights around the waist.
questions.solution: "Too tight" is the correct phrase to use when describing how the dress fits around the waist. "Tights(noun)" means a piece of thin clothing, usually worn by women, that fits tightly from the waist over the legs and feet.  Example: She wore a pair of tights. "Tight(adjective)" means (used about clothes) fitting very closely in a way that is often uncomfortable. We must use an adjective after "too." Correct sentence: The dress is too tight around the waist.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. Mother was watching a movie when the lights were going off.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

Mother was watching a movie when the lights were going off.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.

'were going off' is used incorrectly instead of 'went off'.

The sentence shows a longer action that was interrupted in the past. The interruption is usually a shorter action in the simple past.

The sentence is in the past continuous tense + simple past tense. 'were going off' must be replaced with 'went off'.

Thus the correct sentence would be: Mother was watching a movie when the lights went off.

questions.question: Direction: Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct. Dr. Mark said I can came to his office on Friday or Saturday of next week.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

Dr. Mark said I can came to his office on Friday or Saturday of next week.
questions.solution: The sentence is in the present tense, so "can came" is grammatically incorrect. The modal verb "can" is always followed by the base form of the verb. Example: He can meet me. So, we have to replace "came" with "come" to make it grammatically correct. The correct answer is Option 4. Correct sentence: Dr. Mark said I can come to his office on Friday or Saturday of next week.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Avika understands French, does she ?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.

Avika understands French, does she?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'doesn't she'. 

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
  • A positive statement is followed by a negative question tag.
    • Example: Mary can speak English, can't she?
  • A negative statement is followed by a positive question tag.
    • Example: They aren't funny, are they?
  • In the given sentence, the negative tag of 'does' should be used. 
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4. 
    ​

Correct sentence: Avika understands French, doesn't she?

Additional Information

  • If the sentences start with ''Let's'' (Let us) then ''shall we?'' should be used as a question tag.
    • Example: Let's walk, shall we?

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Indeed, Jack is one of the clever men I have ever met.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.
Indeed, Jack is one of the clever men I have ever met.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2 – "the cleverest".
 
Key Points
  • The sentence uses the phrase "one of the", which must be followed by a superlative degree adjective to compare Jack with a group of people.
  • Among the given options, "the cleverest" is the correct superlative form of “clever.”
  • The use of "most clever" is also a superlative, but when a one-syllable adjective like "clever" has an "-est" form available, it is more natural and preferred in standard usage.
  • Options like “clever” (positive degree) and “cleverer” (comparative degree) are not grammatically appropriate in this sentence structure.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2 – "the cleverest".
 
Correct Sentence: "Indeed, Jack is one of the cleverest men I have ever met."
 
Additional Information
  • Superlative adjectives are used with “one of the…” to show that someone/something belongs to a group characterized by the highest degree of a quality.
  • Examples: “She is one of the best dancers,” “This is one of the most interesting books I’ve read.”

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required select 'No substitution' The assignment was so difficult for Mohit to do all by himself.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required select 'No substitution'

The assignment was so difficult for Mohit to do all by himself.
questions.solution:
• The correct answer is option 1 i.e. 'was too difficult'.
  • Rule: The adverb 'too' should be followed by "adjective + to infinitive(to + V1)". 
    • In the given sentence, the adjective (difficult) is followed by 'to + V1' i.e. 'to + do'.
    • So, according to the rule, the adverb 'so' should be replaced by 'too'.
  • Therefore, the correct sentence is 'The assignment was too difficult for Mohit to do all by himself.'
